title: The stages of a night's sleep
examples: What are the stages of sleep?
How long is a sleep cycle?

stages.label: Light sleep
stages.note: Stage 2: heart slows, body cools

stages.label: REM sleep

explain.say: Sleep is not one steady state. Through the night your brain moves through a cycle of stages, from light sleep to deep sleep to dreaming sleep, and each cycle takes about 90 minutes.

explain.say: After drifting off, you enter light sleep. Your heart slows, your body temperature drops, and your brain waves slow down. About half the night is spent here.

explain.say: Next comes deep sleep, when the brain makes big, slow waves. It is very hard to wake someone now. Deep sleep is when much body repair happens and growth hormone is released.

explain.say: Then comes REM sleep: the eyes dart about under the lids, the brain is busy, and most vivid dreams happen, while the body's muscles stay relaxed. Early cycles have more deep sleep; later ones have more REM.

faq.q: What are the stages of sleep?
faq.a: Sleep has light stages, a deep slow-wave stage and REM, or rapid eye movement, sleep. The brain cycles through them several times a night.
asks: How many stages of sleep are there?

faq.a: In deep sleep the brain produces slow, large waves, breathing and heart rate are slow and steady, and the body releases growth hormone and repairs tissues. People woken from deep sleep often feel groggy.

REM stands for rapid eye movement. In this stage the eyes flick about, the brain is nearly as active as when awake, most vivid dreams happen, and most muscles are temporarily relaxed so you do not act out your dreams.
asks: Why do we dream in REM?

faq.q: How long is a sleep cycle?
faq.a: One cycle through the stages takes about 90 minutes, so a full night usually includes four to six cycles. Deep sleep is longest in the first cycles and REM gets longer towards morning.
asks: How many sleep cycles a night?
Why do I dream more in the morning?

faq.a: In light sleep the heart rate and breathing slow, body temperature falls and brain waves slow down. You can be woken fairly easily, and adults spend about half the night in this stage.

facts: One sleep cycle lasts roughly 90 minutes, and a night usually holds four to six cycles.
Adults spend about a fifth to a quarter of their sleep in REM sleep.

quiz.say: In which sleep stage do most vivid dreams happen?
quiz.why: In REM sleep the brain is very active and the eyes dart about; this is when most vivid dreams occur.

wrong.1: Deep sleep has slow brain waves and few vivid dreams.
wrong.2: Drifting off may bring brief images, but not most vivid dreams.
